Action Plan:
- Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
- Continue ice therapy to the knee as much as possible to reduce pain and swelling.
- Ease up on long runs; if pain worsens or becomes intolerable, stop running and maintain cross-training as advised.
- Refer patient to physiotherapist for comprehensive knee assessment; imaging (e.g., MRI or other) considered only if physiotherapist or exam findings warrant it.
- Prescribe a slightly stronger NSAID for regular use, to replace ibuprofen (do not use with ibuprofen); take with food; dose/route/frequency not documented. Pharmacy to send prescription.
- If red flags develop (persistent swelling/heat/redness, fever, feeling unwell, or knee completely locks), urgent medical evaluation is required.
- Follow-up planned after physiotherapy assessment or sooner if symptoms worsen.

Subjective:
- Chief complaints: Right knee pain with clicking after increased workouts; difficulty running long distances.
- Onset and duration: Symptoms began about 2 weeks ago.
- Activity/exposure: Marathon training; recent longer runs (up to ~7–8 miles, some 4–5 miles, occasional 7-mile runs); gym workouts continued. Recent change primarily in longer run distances.
- Pain features: Pain starts after ~20 minutes of running (around mile 2–3); clicking with knee movement; occasional instability described as “gives way” only mildly; pain worsens with running, not with standing or stairs.
- Side and location: Pain primarily right knee; described as middle of knee with possible movement toward the right side.
- Swelling/effusion: Initial swelling during first run reported; resolved with ice; currently no visible swelling.
- Instability: No true locking; able to straighten and fully flex the knee.
- Mechanical symptoms: Clicking during flexion/extension; intermittent “fluid” sensation reported by patient.
- Neurologic symptoms: Tingling in the right toes once after a run; not persistent.
- Medications: Ibuprofen up to 400 mg as needed; also uses Aleve (naproxen) occasionally (dose/frequency not documented); Vitamin D; Melatonin; occasional Xanax; uses marijuana; no known drug allergies.
- Other medical history: Prior ice hockey injury with a large bruise; Lasik; one emergency/ER visit for a UTI with mistaken stone diagnosis; general “garden variety” illnesses.
- Allergies: None stated.

Objective:
- Right knee: pain localized to middle, with tendency to shift slightly to the right on flexion/extension (patient description; no formal imaging reported).
- Range of motion: Full extension and full flexion.
- Swelling: Currently none; history of transient swelling earlier.
- Instability/locking: No locking reported; no instability noted on exam prompts.
- Tenderness: Not specifically documented on palpation in this transcript.
- Neurologic: Toes tingling once post-run (patient-reported); no persistent numbness described.
- Additional: No current pain in other joints; no redness or color/temperature change noted.

Assessment & Plan:

1) Right knee overuse/knee pain with mechanical symptoms (likely overuse injury with possible patellofemoral or meniscal/cartilage involvement; ACL injury discussed but not diagnosed via video):
   - Plan:
     - Physiotherapy referral for comprehensive knee assessment and management.
     - Imaging (knee) considered if physiotherapist assessment indicates need to evaluate internal structures (cartilage/ligaments).
     - Continue ice therapy; advise on protective measures during activity.
     - Modify running plan (reduce distance/intensity) and avoid activities that exacerbate pain.
     - Consider a stronger NSAID for regular use (to replace ibuprofen) with food; avoid concurrent use with ibuprofen; dose/route/frequency not documented; prescription to be sent to the patient’s pharmacy.
     - If any red flags develop (persistent swelling/heat/redness, fever, unwell feeling, or knee completely locked), seek urgent medical care.

Notes on imaging and referrals: A physiotherapist assessment is prioritized; imaging may follow based on clinical assessment results.
